commits.message:
Add performance review agent and guidelines (#37530)

Adds an agentic workflow that reviews pull requests for performance
issues:
- Pagination and lazy iteration (PagedAsyncIterableIterator,
maxPageSize)
- AbortSignal propagation through async chains and loops
- Memory allocation anti-patterns (deep clones, buffer concat, eager
materialization)
- Streaming and backpressure (highWaterMark, unbounded buffering)
- HTTP efficiency (keep-alive, redundant serialization, batching)
- Retry and polling overhead (backoff, interval floors, retriable
errors)
- Synchronous blocking (sync I/O, ReDoS, CPU-bound without yielding)
- Bundle size impact (large deps, Node-only code in browser paths)
- Async patterns (sequential awaits, unbounded Promise.all)
- Caching and memoization (regex hoisting, unbounded caches)

---------

fix: set min-integrity to unapproved so review agents can read PRs (#37841)

The default integrity filter requires PR content to be "approved" before
agents can read it. Since review agents need to review PRs **before**
approval, this blocks them from reading the PR diff.

Observed in [Dash's review of
#37835](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-js/pull/37835#pullrequestreview-4010990873):

> 🔒 Integrity filter blocked 2 items
> `pull_request_read`: has lower integrity than agent requires. The
agent cannot read data with integrity below "approved".

Adds `min-integrity: unapproved` to all 6 review agents' GitHub toolset
config.

Also recompiles lock files with gh-aw v0.64.0.

---------

+## Step 2.5 — Micro-Benchmark Verification
+
+For any finding that involves a **performance optimization** (new or
+modified), write and run a quick Node.js micro-benchmark using `bash`
+to **measure** the actual impact before posting the finding. This
+includes changes you want to flag AND changes you want to confirm as
+beneficial. Follow the micro-benchmark methodology in the guidelines
+(Section 12).
+
+**When to benchmark:**
+
+- The PR adds a fast path, cache, or heuristic to skip expensive work
+- The PR replaces a polling mechanism with an event-driven approach
+- You identify an allocation pattern and want to suggest an alternative
+- You want to verify whether an optimization is net-positive or
+  net-negative across representative inputs
+
+**When NOT to benchmark:**
+
+- The issue is structural (missing AbortSignal, unbounded buffer, no
+  pagination) — these are correctness/design issues, not speed claims
+- The change is self-evidently beneficial (removing dead code, fixing
+  a quadratic loop to linear)
+- The affected code path is not hot (called fewer than 1,000 times per
+  second in typical usage)
+
+**How to benchmark:**
+
+1. Write a standalone `bench.mjs` file using the template from the
+   guidelines document (Section 12).
+2. Run it with `node bench.mjs` via the bash tool.
+3. Include the benchmark results as a markdown table in your review
+   comment for that finding.
+4. **Assess materiality**: compare the absolute per-operation cost
+   to the I/O overhead on the same code path. A 100 ns saving on a
+   path that includes a 5 ms network call is noise.
+5. Clean up: remove the benchmark file after collecting results.
+
+**Optimization justification:**
+
+Before endorsing or only suggesting improvements to a new optimization, also apply the
+optimization justification checklist from the guidelines (Section 13):
+- Search for existing alternatives that already solve the same problem
+- Assess complexity vs measured benefit
+- Check for regressions across different input classes
+- Question module-level state (caches, memoization)
+

commits.message:
Switch agentic workflows from pull_request_target to pull_request with fork guard (#38035)

## Security: Replace `pull_request_target` with `pull_request` in
agentic workflows

Switches all 7 agentic review workflows (archie, dash, dexter,
mgmt-review, scribe, sentinel, tester) from `pull_request_target` to
`pull_request` to reduce their privilege surface.

### Why this matters

`pull_request_target` runs in the **base branch context** with full
access to repository secrets and a write-enabled `GITHUB_TOKEN` — even
for PRs from forks. This is an unnecessary privilege escalation for
workflows that only perform read-only AI-powered code reviews.

Using `pull_request` instead follows the [principle of least
privilege](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#understanding-the-risk-of-script-injections):
no secrets are exposed for fork PRs and the token is read-only.

### What changed

1. **Trigger**: `pull_request_target` → `pull_request` across all 7
workflow `.md` and `.lock.yml` files.
2. **Fork guard**: Added `github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork ==
false` to job conditions so workflows skip gracefully on forked PRs
(where secrets are unavailable) instead of failing.
3. **Removed workaround**: Deleted the `pull_request_target` checkout
instructions from `mgmt-review.md` that were only needed because the old
trigger checked out the base branch instead of the PR branch.

### References

- [GitHub Security Lab — Preventing pwn
requests](https://securitylab.github.com/resources/github-actions-preventing-pwn-requests/)
- [GitHub Docs — Security hardening for GitHub
Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions)
- [GitHub Blog — `pull_request_target` and branch protection
changes](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-11-07-actions-pull_request_target-and-environment-branch-protections-changes/)

### Packages impacted

None — workflow/CI changes only.

---------

Co-authored-by: copilot-swe-agent[bot] <198982749+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: deyaaeldeen <6074665+deyaaeldeen@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.message:
Fix race condition in label-triggered review workflows (#38093)

### Problem

When multiple review labels (e.g. `docs-review-needed` +
`test-review-needed`) are applied to a PR simultaneously, review
workflows silently fail to run.

**Root cause**: GitHub Actions `pull_request: types: [labeled]` fires
for *any* label — there is no way to filter by specific label at the
trigger level. So each label event triggers **all 7** review workflows.
The `if:` condition on each job correctly skips non-matching labels, but
the concurrency group (`gh-aw-<workflow>-<PR#>`) is evaluated first.

When the same workflow is triggered twice in quick succession (once per
label event), `cancel-in-progress: true` cancels the first run — which
may be the one whose label actually matched. The second run then skips
because its label does not match. Net result: the workflow never
completes.

**Example**: On
[#37993](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-js/pull/37993) at
`2026-04-10T15:32:11Z`, Documentation Review was cancelled by a
`test-review-needed` label event and never ran.

### Fix

Include `github.event.label.name` in the concurrency group for all 7
label-triggered review workflows.

- **Same workflow + same label** → same group → `cancel-in-progress`
works as intended
- **Same workflow + different label** → different groups → no
interference

### Why not make the trigger more specific?

GitHub Actions does not support filtering `labeled` events by label name
at the trigger level. Filtering can only happen via job-level `if:`
conditions, which execute after the concurrency group is resolved. The
concurrency group fix is the only viable approach.

### Affected workflows

`archie`, `dash`, `dexter`, `mgmt-review`, `scribe`, `sentinel`,
`tester`

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
commits.attribution_evidence: no supported agent signature in commit metadata

+concurrency:
+  group: "gh-aw-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref || github.run_id }}-${{ github.event.label.name || '' }}"
+  cancel-in-progress: true

commits.message:
Enable fork PR support and fix race condition in review workflows (#38105)

## What

Switch all 7 review workflows (archie, dash, dexter, mgmt-review,
scribe, sentinel, tester) from `pull_request` to `pull_request_target`
to enable reviews on fork PRs. This follows the pattern established in
[azure-rest-api-specs#42268](https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/pull/42268).

## Changes

- **`pull_request` → `pull_request_target`** with `forks: ["*"]` —
allows workflows to run on fork PRs
- **`workflow_dispatch`** with `item_number` input — enables manual
re-runs
- **Label removal step** in `on.steps` (pre-activation) — removes the
trigger label since `label_command` isn't used with
`pull_request_target`
- **Removed `fork == false` guard** from `if:` conditions — no longer
needed since the label gate (only collaborators can apply labels)
provides the security boundary
- **Label-aware concurrency group** — includes `github.event.label.name`
in the concurrency key to prevent a race condition where applying
multiple review labels simultaneously causes one workflow run to cancel
another (see #38093)

## Security

`pull_request_target` runs from the base branch context with write token
access. This is safe because:
1. Only collaborators can apply trigger labels (label gate)
2. The workflows read PR content via API calls, not by checking out fork
code
3. No untrusted code from the fork is executed

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
commits.attribution_evidence: no supported agent signature in commit metadata

feat(workflows): Add 3-state label system for review workflows (#38439)

## Summary

Updates all 7 review agent workflows to use a 3-label state system for
better UX:

| State | Label | Description |
|-------|-------|-------------|
| Request | `*-needed` | User adds to request review |
| Running | `*-in-progress` | Auto-swapped when workflow starts |
| Complete | `*-added` | Auto-swapped when review finishes |

## Motivation

Previously, the trigger label was removed immediately when the workflow
started, which was confusing during long-running reviews. Users couldn't
tell if the review was in progress or had been cancelled.

Addresses:
https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-js/pull/38105#discussion_r3193705875

## Changes

### Workflows Updated
- archie (architecture review)
- dash (performance review)
- dexter (dependency review)
- mgmt-review (management SDK review)
- scribe (documentation review)
- sentinel (security review)
- tester (test review)

### New Labels Created
14 new labels (7 `-in-progress` + 7 `-added`) have already been created
in the repository.

## Testing

To test, add any `*-needed` label to a PR and observe:
1. Label swaps to `*-in-progress` when workflow starts
2. Label swaps to `*-added` when review completes

Adopt copilot-requests: write permission for agentic workflows (#38944)

## What

Adds the `copilot-requests: write` permission to the frontmatter of all
11 GitHub Agentic Workflows (gh-aw) and regenerates their compiled
`.lock.yml` files.

## Why

This is the [recommended Copilot inference
authentication](https://github.github.com/gh-aw/reference/auth/#copilot-requests-write-permission)
for gh-aw. With `copilot-requests: write` present:

- gh-aw uses the **built-in GitHub Actions token** for Copilot inference
- no PAT required.
- The `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` secret is no longer needed for inference
(tokens are minted per-run and auto-revoked).
- Billing flows through the organization''s Copilot subscription rather
than an individual''s quota.

## Changes

Each workflow''s frontmatter gains a single line:

```yaml
permissions:
  ...
  copilot-requests: write
```

Recompiling with `gh aw compile` (v0.77.5, matching the existing lock
files) produces the corresponding `.lock.yml` updates:

- `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN }}` ->
`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}`
- adds `copilot-requests: write` to the relevant job `permissions`
blocks
- adds `S2STOKENS: true` to the agent/detection env
- drops the now-unnecessary `Validate COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN secret` step
and related secret-verification plumbing

Workflows updated: archie, dash, dexter, docs-consistency-check,
fix-test-failures, issue-triage, mgmt-review, scribe, sentinel, tester,
upgrade-agentic-workflows.

## Notes

- Lock files were regenerated with the same compiler version (`v0.77.5`)
already recorded in their metadata, so the diff is limited to the auth
change.
- A pre-existing manual edit in `mgmt-review.lock.yml` (a
`continue-on-error: true` on the *Checkout PR branch* step) was
preserved to keep this PR scoped strictly to the permission change.

Generated with Copilot CLI

commits.message:
Updating permissions for agentic workflows (#39071)

## Updating permissions for agentic workflows

Adds the `copilot-requests: write` permission to the GitHub Agentic
Workflow definitions and recompiles their generated lock files.

### What changed
- Added `copilot-requests: write` under `permissions:` in each agentic
workflow `.md` source file.
- Recompiled every corresponding `.lock.yml` via `gh aw compile` so the
generated output matches the source.

As a result of recompiling, the workflows now rely on the
`copilot-requests: write` permission instead of the
`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` secret, so the lock files drop the
`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` secret reference and its validation step.

### Affected workflows
- agent-observability
- archie
- dash
- dexter
- docs-consistency-check
- fix-test-failures
- issue-triage
- mgmt-guidance
- mgmt-review
- scribe
- sentinel
- tester
- upgrade-agentic-workflows

### Checklist
- [x] Add `copilot-requests: write` permission to workflow `.md` sources
- [x] Recompile `.lock.yml` files from their `.md` counterparts
- [x] Add PR description

[engsys] Update gh-aw to latest version and enable new billing option (#39089)

This PR updates gh-aw to the latest version (0.81.3) and updates our
permissions to use the new `copilot-requests: write` permission per
https://github.github.com/gh-aw/reference/auth/#copilot-requests-write-permission

Previous attempts at this failed because the version was outdated.
During my efforts to upgrade this, I also noticed that gh-aw's MCP
server does not seem to work with copilot (fails to initialize) so I
have removed that entry from mcp.json.

As proof that this *actually* works this time (unlike in #39071 and
#38944) I was able to run a successful agent against the PR branch:
https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-js/actions/runs/28194833437/job/83518875360
